newsitem.title: USA: Ford gains flexibility with skilled workers.
newsitem.headline: Ford gains flexibility with skilled workers.

text.p: Ford Motor Co would for the first time gain national flexibility on how it deploys its skilled workforce to make the company more competitive, according to terms of its tentative agreement with the United Auto Workers union.

According to a union summary of the contract, new guidelines allow plants to develop skilled trade work groups that would "allow the plant to grow the business, attract new work, or become more competitve," as long as the union agrees to a change in work rules.
Previously, only some of the Ford plants have had such an arrangement.
UAW spokesman Karl Mantyla said the agreement moves toward a more modern operating system. "It's basically a more flexible way of utilizing people."
Analysts were not sure how much of a win the flexibility issue is for Ford in a contract that is rich in economic gains and job guarantees for UAW workers.
"It could be significant, depending on how much quantification and how much teeth it has," said David Healy, analyst at Burnham Securities.
